description: HUMAN error-analysis drops. Archived under drop/specs/ and drop/docker-images/. Use drop_task.py. LLM drops go in eval/data-pipeline/curate/out/drop.json.

dropped.reason: Problem statement frames repro as requiring home-assistant/core (or says it cannot be reproduced outside HA). Eval only has the pytest checkout, so agents chase an unavailable dependency / DIY repro that never fails, and do not find the real main.py Directory-reuse fix. Drop per curate policy: external-repo repro requirement.

Human error-analysis exclude: problem statement is too vague for the model to reproduce the specific hidden-test case. Symptom: agent repros always succeed, so it cannot locate the real bug, gets confused, then drifts to unrelated failures.

Human review: the problem statement concatenates four independent defects (.env quoting, UTF-16 sanitation, auxiliary key_env resolution, and HERMES_HOME prompt paths). The gold patch modifies all four areas, but FAIL_TO_PASS covers only the first two. Agents are asked to solve unscored requirements, so this is not one coherent and fully validated task.

Human review: the core request is Desktop/Electron readiness. The gold patch changes both the Electron probe and backend health endpoint, but FAIL_TO_PASS contains only two Python health-endpoint tests. An implementation that never fixes Desktop can pass, while other fixes explicitly allowed by the statement can fail.

Human review: the core request is to ship a fixed SQLite in the Docker image. A Docker runtime regression test exists in test_patch but is absent from FAIL_TO_PASS; scored tests only assert doctor hint text. The task can pass without correcting the SQLite library shipped in the image.

Human review: the statement requests macOS Tauri installer and launcher marker behavior. The gold patch spans Rust, Electron, and install.sh, but FAIL_TO_PASS scores only install.sh marker helpers. A direct Rust installer fix may fail, and passing the scored shell tests does not validate launcher behavior.

Human review: the statement allows moving the pycache sweep before lazy refresh or launching refresh with bytecode disabled, but FAIL_TO_PASS is coupled to new checkout-fingerprint and bytecode-helper APIs introduced by the gold patch. Valid stated solutions would fail, and no integration FAIL_TO_PASS verifies update ordering.

Human review: the statement explicitly accepts a warning, bulk repin, confirmation prompt, or softer failure. The sole FAIL_TO_PASS requires one narrow model.name configuration warning, so multiple valid UX fixes are rejected and the broader expected behavior is untested.

Human review: the statement concatenates MCP call_id overflow and reasoning-item id overflow. The gold patch and sole FAIL_TO_PASS address only call_id, leaving the second requested defect unvalidated and the task scope ambiguous.

Human review: the claimed slow-onset SQLite corruption is not reproducible or tested; F2P only forces one preselected PASSIVE-checkpoint implementation and logging, rejecting other fixes the prompt explicitly permits.

Human review: F2P requires an unmentioned resolve_gateway_liveness/GatewayLiveness architecture, while the direct profile-path fix allowed by the prompt would fail; the Kanban half of the core request has no behavioral F2P.
Human review: the Windows stale-lock task is scored only by dispatch to a named helper; real lock recovery is skipped/unscored, so a no-op helper passes and a correct inline implementation fails.

Human review: the prompt asks for fatal-adapter recovery after transient outage, but F2P only checks watcher task-handle bookkeeping; no test exercises adapter failure, upstream recovery, reconnect, or gateway status.
